config.title: Oldest Restaurants in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: Which Berlin restaurants and pubs are genuinely old, what the famous dates really mean, and how to plan an evening around them.

items.q: What is the oldest restaurant in Berlin?
items.a: **Zur letzten Instanz on Waisenstraße**, with a first documented mention in 1561 and a run as an inn dated to 1621. The honest footnote is that the war wrecked the building and **today's room dates from the 1963 reconstruction**. The tiled stove and the medieval city wall beside the terrace are the genuinely old parts.

**The story is, the building is not.** The 1571 tavern stood on Fischerstraße on the Fischerinsel and was destroyed in 1943. The inn you visit in the Nikolaiviertel is a **faithful replica built in 1987** for Berlin's 750th birthday, open daily from 12:00 to 22:00.

items.q: Which Berlin pubs still have their original old interiors?
items.a: Four survivors stand out: **E. & M. Leydicke** in Schöneberg (1877, same family, own fruit wines), **Wilhelm Hoeck 1892** in Charlottenburg (original carved bar room), **Max & Moritz** in Kreuzberg (listed 1902 Jugendstil rooms) and **Henne** in Kreuzberg (1908 wood-panelled room, famous milk-fed half chicken).

items.q: Do I need to reserve at Berlin's historic restaurants?
items.a: **At the restaurants, yes; at the pubs, no.** Henne books out a day or two ahead and Zur letzten Instanz fills at dinner, while Wilhelm Hoeck, Leydicke and Zum Nußbaum are walk-ins. Watch the closing days: the Instanz closes Sunday, Henne closes Monday, Max & Moritz closes Tuesday, and Konnopke's closes Sunday and Monday.

items.q: What is Berlin's oldest beer garden?
items.a: **Prater Garten on Kastanienallee in Prenzlauer Berg, pouring in the same courtyard since 1837.** It is seasonal: daily from noon from roughly April to September, weather permitting, with the adjoining tavern carrying the winter.
